title: Unique compatible section lift of quotient morphisms
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ a quasi-coherent ideal, and $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ coherent modules [pqf-def-coherent]. Use the completion quotient systems and projections of [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module], with positive levels $n+1$. Let $\mathcal H=\mathcal Hom(\mathcal G,\mathcal F)$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom], and suppose given maps $e_n:\mathcal H/\mathcal I^{n+1}\mathcal H\to\mathcal Hom(\mathcal G/\mathcal I^{n+1}\mathcal G,\mathcal F/\mathcal I^{n+1}\mathcal F)$ whose composites with $q_{n+1}^{\mathcal H}$ and precomposition with $q_{n+1}^{\mathcal G}$ equal postcomposition with $q_{n+1}^{\mathcal F}$. For every family $t_n:\mathcal G/\mathcal I^{n+1}\mathcal G\to\mathcal F/\mathcal I^{n+1}\mathcal F$ commuting with all transition maps, there exists exactly one compatible family of global sections $s_n$ of $\mathcal H/\mathcal I^{n+1}\mathcal H$ whose images under $\Gamma(e_n)$ and the global internal-Hom identification equal $t_n$ for every $n$.

proof.text: For any family e satisfying the factorization equation, its restriction on affine sections is the canonical quotient evaluation map: the affine quotient projection is surjective and precomposition with the source quotient is injective by finite-level factorization. (Affine opens: the modules.) Let $U\subseteq X$ be an affine open and $A=\mathcal O_X(U)$, so $(U,\mathcal O_X|_U)\cong\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. As $X$ is locally Noetherian, $A$ is Noetherian [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth]; so $U$ is a Noetherian scheme. Put $I=\mathcal I(U)$; as $\mathcal I|_U$ is quasi-coherent, the counit $\widetilde I\to\mathcal I|_U$ is an isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] (3), so $(U,\mathcal I|_U)$ is the situation of [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-affine] for $(A,I)$. The sheaves $\mathcal F,\mathcal G,\mathcal H$ are coherent ([lem-weil-pbc-coherent-sheaf-hom-coherent] for $\mathcal H$), hence quasi-coherent of finite type [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth], so $M=\mathcal F(U)$, $N=\mathcal G(U)$ and $\mathcal H(U)$ are finitely generated $A$-modules [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine] (a), and $\mathcal F_n(U)=M/I^nM$, $\mathcal G_n(U)=N/I^nN$, $\mathcal H_n(U)=\mathcal H(U)/I^n\mathcal H(U)$ with $q_n(U)$ the quotient maps [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections] (2). By full faithfulness of $\Gamma(U,-)$ on quasi-coherent modules over the affine $U$ ([lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] (1),(3): $\alpha\mapsto\Gamma(U,\alpha)$ is the adjunction bijection composed with the counit isomorphism), $\mathcal H(U)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_U}(\mathcal G|_U,\mathcal F|_U)\to H:=\operatorname{Hom}_A(N,M)$, $\varphi\mapsto\varphi_U$, is an $A$-linear bijection (so $H$ is a finitely generated $A$-module), and likewise $\mathcal Hom(\mathcal G_n,\mathcal F_n)(U)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_A(N/I^nN,M/I^nM)$. Under these identifications $\mathcal H_n(U)=H/I^nH$ and $e_n(U)$ of step 1 is $h\bmod I^nH\mapsto\bar h_n$, where $\bar h_n(x\bmod I^nN)=h(x)\bmod I^nM$ (evaluate on sections over $U$, where $q^{\mathcal H}_n(U)$ is surjective). Hence $\varprojlim_n\Gamma(U,\mathcal H_n)=\varprojlim_nH/I^nH=H^\wedge$.

proof.text: (Affine opens: reduction to modules over $A^\wedge$.) Keep the notation of step 2 and let $E:\mathit{Coh}(U,\mathcal I|_U)\to\mathrm{Mod}^{fg}(A^\wedge)$, $(\mathcal P_n)\mapsto\varprojlim_n\Gamma(U,\mathcal P_n)$, $(\alpha_n)\mapsto\varprojlim_n\Gamma(U,\alpha_n)$, be the equivalence of [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-affine] (2); in particular $E$ is bijective on Hom sets. By step 2, $E(\mathcal G^\wedge|_U)=\varprojlim N/I^nN=N^\wedge$ and $E(\mathcal F^\wedge|_U)=M^\wedge$ (with $A^\wedge$ acting componentwise), and $E\circ\Phi_U:H^\wedge\to\operatorname{Hom}_{A^\wedge}(N^\wedge,M^\wedge)$ is $$\beta:(h_n\bmod I^nH)_n\longmapsto\big((x_n\bmod I^nN)_n\mapsto(h_n(x_n)\bmod I^nM)_n\big).$$ Hence $\Phi_U$ is bijective if and only if $\beta$ is. Note that $\beta$ is $A^\wedge$-linear: $\beta((a_n)_n(h_n)_n)$ and $(a_n)_n\beta((h_n)_n)$ both send $(x_n)$ to $(a_nh_n(x_n))_n$; and for $h\in H$, $\beta(\iota_H(h))=h^\wedge:(x_n)_n\mapsto(h(x_n))_n$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0882 (lemma-completion-internal-hom, line 6438), proof: 'The statement of the lemma becomes the statement H^ = Hom_{A^}(M^, N^) via the equivalence of Lemma 087W'

proof.text: (Affine opens: $\beta$ is bijective.) $A$ is Noetherian and $N$, $M$, $H$ are finitely generated $A$-modules (step 2). By [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-module-tensor] (2) the $A^\wedge$-linear maps $c_P:A^\wedge\otimes_AP\to P^\wedge$, $a\otimes x\mapsto a\,\iota_P(x)$, are bijective for $P=N,M,H$. The ring map $A\to A^\wedge$ is flat [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-completion-flat], and $N$ is finitely generated over the Noetherian $A$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-hom-finitely-presented] the map $\theta:A^\wedge\otimes_AH\to\operatorname{Hom}_{A^\wedge}(A^\wedge\otimes_AN,A^\wedge\otimes_AM)$, $a\otimes h\mapsto a(\mathrm{id}\otimes h)$, is bijective. Let $\gamma:\operatorname{Hom}_{A^\wedge}(A^\wedge\otimes_AN,A^\wedge\otimes_AM)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{A^\wedge}(N^\wedge,M^\wedge)$, $f\mapsto c_M\circ f\circ c_N^{-1}$, a bijection. Both $\beta\circ c_H$ and $\gamma\circ\theta$ are $A^\wedge$-linear (step 3), and $A^\wedge\otimes_AH$ is generated as an $A^\wedge$-module by the $1\otimes h$; on these, $\beta(c_H(1\otimes h))=\beta(\iota_H(h))=h^\wedge$ (step 3) and $\gamma(\theta(1\otimes h))=c_M\circ(\mathrm{id}\otimes h)\circ c_N^{-1}=h^\wedge$ by the naturality $h^\wedge\circ c_N=c_M\circ(\mathrm{id}\otimes h)$ [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-module-tensor] (1). Hence $\beta=\gamma\circ\theta\circ c_H^{-1}$ is bijective, and by step 3 so is $\Phi_U$, for every affine open $U\subseteq X$. (This is Stacks' chain $H^\wedge=H\otimes_AA^\wedge=\operatorname{Hom}_{A^\wedge}(N\otimes_AA^\wedge,M\otimes_AA^\wedge)=\operatorname{Hom}_{A^\wedge}(N^\wedge,M^\wedge)$, with the check that it is the map $\beta$.)

proof.text: Apply local bijectivity to the given compatible family t, glue the unique local inverse section families as in the parent step 5, and use local injectivity to prove global uniqueness. (From affine opens to $X$.) The affine opens of $X$ form a basis of its topology, and $\mathcal H_n$ and $\mathcal Hom(\mathcal G_n,\mathcal F_n)$ are sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Injectivity of $\Phi$: if $\Phi(s)=\Phi(s')$ then for every affine open $U$, $\Phi_U(s|_U)=\Phi(s)|_U=\Phi(s')|_U=\Phi_U(s'|_U)$ (step 1 (e)), so $s_n|_U=s'_n|_U$ for all $n$ (step 4), and $s_n=s'_n$ as the affine opens cover $X$. Surjectivity: let $\alpha=(\alpha_n)$ be a morphism $\mathcal G^\wedge\to\mathcal F^\wedge$. For each affine open $U$ choose (step 4) $t^U\in\varprojlim_n\Gamma(U,\mathcal H_n)$ with $\Phi_U(t^U)=\alpha|_U$. For affine opens $U,V$ and an affine open $W\subseteq U\cap V$, $\Phi_W(t^U|_W)=\alpha|_W=\Phi_W(t^V|_W)$ (step 1 (e), applied on $U$ and on $V$), so $t^U_n|_W=t^V_n|_W$ (step 4); such $W$ cover $U\cap V$, so $t^U_n$ and $t^V_n$ agree on $U\cap V$ and glue to $s_n\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal H_n)$. The relation $t_n(s_{n+1})=s_n$ holds on every affine $U$, hence on $X$; so $s=(s_n)\in\varprojlim_n\Gamma(X,\mathcal H_n)$, and $\Phi(s)_n$ and $\alpha_n$ are sections of $\mathcal Hom(\mathcal G_n,\mathcal F_n)$ with the same restriction $\Phi_U(t^U)_n=\alpha_n|_U$ to every affine $U$, hence equal. So $\Phi$ is bijective.
